answer:
**Final hypothesis (English, data-grounded):**

In a PCA performed on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices (capital.csv: BCE 500–4300, 12 capital variables as interpolated Z-scores), the first principal component (PC1, 30.3% of the total variance), oriented so that metal valuables are positive (CopperGold, loading +0.41), contrasts the accumulation of prestige/monetary capital — CopperGold (+0.41), PotteryDecoration (+0.38), Depot/hoards (+0.34), HatchetSword (+0.30), Dagger (+0.27), MonumentSize (+0.24), HouseSize (+0.23), MonumentCount (+0.20) — against utilitarian/agricultural and exchange items that load negatively — PotteryForm (−0.35), AxesCelts (−0.24), Amber (−0.24), Sickle (−0.15).

- The **Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE)** is characterized by a strongly and steadily **negative** PC1: all five century-slices are below zero, with a phase mean of ≈ −1.37 (≈ 0.7σ below the whole-series mean of 0), and the score **declines** through the phase from ≈ −0.58 (3400 BCE) to ≈ −1.78 (3000 BCE), i.e. a deepening negative trough in which metal valuables, hoards, prestige weapons, decorated pottery, houses and monuments are at (or near) their minimum while pottery-form diversity, axes/celts, sickles and amber are comparatively high.
- The **Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE)** is characterized by a still **negative but rising** PC1: all seven century-slices remain below zero (mean ≈ −1.12, ≈ 0.6σ below the series mean) yet the score **recovers** from ≈ −1.50 (2900 BCE) to ≈ −0.41 (2300 BCE), an upward trend back toward the series mean — a phase of gradual renewed capital accumulation (metals, decorated pottery, hoards, prestige/monumental capital) after the Middle Neolithic minimum, without yet crossing into the positive range.

Cross-check with per-capital PC1s (corrected mapping, each oriented by its dominant loading):
- Symbolic capital PC1 (Dagger +0.66, HouseSize +0.57, HatchetSword +0.49; 54.4% var.): weakly negative, declining in MN (mean −0.17; +0.57→−0.49) and negative with a slight rise in YN (mean −0.47).
- Social capital PC1 (CopperGold +0.68, MonumentCount +0.66, Amber −0.31; 48.6% var.): clearly negative and declining in MN (mean −0.65, all slices <0) but turns near-zero/positive and rising in YN (mean +0.22).
- Cultural capital PC1 (PotteryDecoration +0.71 vs PotteryForm −0.71; 72.5% var.): deeply negative in both phases (MN −0.92, YN −0.81; i.e., high pottery-form diversity and low decoration), slightly less extreme in YN.
- Economic capital PC1 (Depot +0.72, AxesCelts −0.56, MonumentSize +0.36, Sickle +0.17; 35.9% var.): negative in both phases and even deeper in YN (MN mean −0.75, YN mean −1.14), i.e., persistently low hoards/monument size with relatively high axes/celts.

**Synthesis:** both phases occupy the negative side of the capital-forms PC1, but the Middle Neolithic is the deeper, declining trough of the two (minimum of capital-accumulation intensity, ~3000 BCE), whereas the Younger Neolithic, though still negative, shows a rising/recovering PC1, driven above all by the social-capital component (copper/gold, monument count) turning positive, while cultural and economic capital remain depressed.

payload.hypothesis: In a PCA on the forms of capital performed on hundred-year time slices (capital.csv, BCE 500-4300, 12 interpolated Z variables), PC1 (30.3% of variance; oriented with CopperGold positive, loading +0.41) contrasts valuable/prestige accumulation - CopperGold, PotteryDecoration, Depot, HatchetSword, Dagger, MonumentSize, HouseSize, MonumentCount (positive loadings) - against PotteryForm, AxesCelts, Amber, Sickle (negative loadings). Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE): PC1 strongly and steadily negative - all 5 century-slices <0, mean ~ -1.37 (~0.7 SD below series mean), declining from ~ -0.58 (3400 BCE) to ~ -1.78 (3000 BCE), a deepening trough in capital accumulation. Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE): PC1 still negative (all 7 slices <0, mean ~ -1.12) but rising, recovering from ~ -1.50 (2900 BCE) to ~ -0.41 (2300 BCE) toward the series mean - gradual renewed accumulation (led by social capital: CopperGold/MonumentCount turning positive) without reaching the positive range.
payload.workflow: 1) Parse capital.csv (comma-decimals), drop group/color; 39 hundred-year slices BCE 500-4300. 2) Define phases by group column: MN=BCE 3400-3000 (5 slices), Younger Neolithic=BCE 2900-2300 (7 slices). 3) Correlation-matrix PCA on 12 capital variables -> overall PC1; per-capital PCAs using corrected mapping (Symbolic=HatchetSword+Dagger+HouseSize; Social=CopperGold+Amber+MonumentCount; Cultural=PotteryForm+PotteryDecoration; Economic=Depot+Sickle+AxesCelts+MonumentSize). 4) Orient PC1 signs by dominant loading (+). 5) Per phase compute mean, min/max, fraction negative, first/last, OLS slope per 100 BCE, r2; compare vs full-series mean (0, sigma=1.908). 6) Optional context: correlation of overall PC1 with pollen openness (r~0.71-0.73).
